messages:
emily: Alert: multiple restore jobs failing with KMS AccessDenied. restoring tenant backups fails at unwrap step.
emily: log snippet: 
```
2026-04-02T12:34:21Z ERROR backup-restore: kms:Decrypt failed for envelopeKeyId arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/abcdef on object snapshots/prod/tenant-21/2026-04-02.snap: AccessDeniedException
```
raj: which principal is hitting KMS? do we have the grant id?
nina: audit search shows calls from service principal arn:aws:sts::123456789:assumed-role/backup-restore-role/session-xyz at 2755549000-2755550000. security_bot: audit link -> https://internal.logs/redwood/search?q=kms%20Decrypt%20arn%3Aaws%3Akms%3Aus-east-1%3A123456789%3Akey%2Fabcdef
tom: we rotated the envelope-key grant manager yesterday as part of the DB migration that pruned stale grants. there was a migration script that removed grant records older than 90 days. could be related.
emily: timeline: grant prune migration ran 2755548000. restore failures started showing ~2755549200.
dave: we already have 3 customer tickets "restore failed: cannot decrypt backup" queued. support is holding on escalations.
raj: KMS grants are separate objects in AWS KMS. If we removed grant references in our DB but didn't revoke the physical grant, it shouldn't break existing decrypts unless we also removed the grant via the KMS API. did the migration call KMS:RetireGrant/CancelKeyDeletion?
tom: migration logged calls to an internal cleanup service that called kms:RevokeGrant for grants listed as orphaned. I pushed that change out during a maintenance window to reduce entitlement sprawl.
nina: so we likely revoked grants that were still in use by the backup-restore-role. we should check the grant ids attached to the envelope metadata to confirm.
security_bot: quick query -> found 14 distinct envelope metadata entries referencing grants that were revoked between 2755547000-2755548200. Report: https://internal.tasks/scan/scan-9982
emily: mitigation plan: 1) stop further revoke jobs (rollback cleanup) 2) reissue short-lived grants for the backup-restore-role scoped to the specific envelope-ids 3) attempt replay of failed restores once grants in place 4) notify affected tenants and open incident.
raj: reissuing: we can call kms:CreateGrant with granteePrincipal backup-restore-role and operations: ['Decrypt','GenerateDataKey']. but ensure grants are constrained to the envelope key and have a reasonable retirement date.
tom: we need approvals from security and legal before automating re-granting for customer-owned envelope keys. some tenants used CMKs they control. list of affected tenants looks like 6 internal + 8 customer managed.
nina: for customer-managed keys we must coordinate with tenant ops and ask them to re-grant or rotate. we can't unilaterally create grants on CMKs we don't own.
emily: immediate containment: pause the cleanup job (tom done), create emergency grants for our internal CMKs so internal restores can proceed (raj to run), run a targeted restore replay for the 14 failed jobs.
raj: executing CreateGrant for key/abcdef now with constraints to encryptionContext {"snapshot":"tenant-21"} and operations Decrypt, GenerateDataKey. command: `aws kms create-grant --key-id arn:aws:kms:... --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::123456789:role/backup-restore-role --operations Decrypt GenerateDataKey --constraints EncryptionContextSubset={snapshot=tenant-21}`
security_bot: audit: create-grant calls emitted at 2755550050 by raj.
dave: support: I'll respond to the 3 tickets with a templated message that we're investigating and expect a resolution in ~1h.
emily: verification: raj, once grants created, try a test decrypt against one of the failed snapshots and report result.
raj: test result: decrypt succeeded for tenant-21 snapshot after new grant. replayed 1 failed job -> success.
emily: good. action items: - tom: revert or make cleanup job safer (don't auto-revoke grants with last-used < 90d without cross-check) - nina: produce a safe list of CMKs we cannot auto-touch and update runbook - raj: build a one-click grant reissue tool for emergency restores with audit logging - emily: draft customer communication and incident postmortem.
tom: will add a pre-check to the prune job to consult live last-used data from KMS (if available) and to skip keys referenced by active envelope metadata.
nina: also add stronger CI tests: simulate copy of snapshots and verify envelope metadata still maps to active grants before any revoke.
emily: severity P1 due to customer impact. paging oncall and legal to review customer-managed key cases.
security_bot: linked tickets: https://internal.tickets/INC-1122, https://internal.tickets/INC-1123 ; legal loop: https://internal.comms/legal/inc-1122
raj: I'll run a scan to enumerate all snapshots referencing revoked grants and produce a CSV for owner outreach.
emily: thanks all. followup meeting in 45m to finalize postmortem. if anyone sees unusual access patterns to the snapshot objects, tag me and @oncall. :pray:
